title: Trump: Jacob Wohl is caught trying to stop Democrats from voting in 2020
description_short: Trump: Jacob Wohl is caught trying to stop Democrats from voting in 2020
description_medium: A fundraising document for Jacob Wohl’s Arlington Center for Political Intelligence reportedly sought $1 million and described producing fake news for profit and election interference. The supplied account does not show that the proposal was funded or carried out, or identify a specific plan to prevent Democrats from voting. The headline’s claim therefore remains unsupported by the available details.
description_long: The supplied account says The Daily Beast obtained a fundraising document for Jacob Wohl’s Arlington Center for Political Intelligence in May 2019. The document reportedly sought $1 million and described an operation that could mass-produce fake news for profit and election interference. That pitch, if accurately summarized, documents a proposed political influence venture and its stated ambitions; it does not by itself establish that the money was raised or the operation was launched. The available details do not identify specific Democratic voters or districts as targets, describe a concrete effort to obstruct registration or voting, or show that anyone was prevented from voting in 2020. The record’s headline says Wohl was caught trying to stop Democrats from voting, a stronger claim than the supplied account supports. The linked TrumpFile page was inaccessible in a focused read, and the original fundraising document is not included here. A careful account can describe the reported proposal, but evidence of implementation or a specific voter-suppression plan is needed before treating the headline’s assertion as established.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: Jacob Wohl is caught trying to stop Democrats from voting in 2020
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: Jacob Wohl is caught trying to stop Democrats from voting in 2020

notes: Needs context: the available account describes a fundraising pitch but does not establish that it was implemented or that it targeted Democratic voters’ ability to vote; the focused TrumpFile page returned HTTP 202.
Proposed correction: describe the document as a proposed influence campaign unless the original document or contemporaneous reporting substantiates voter suppression and implementation.

title: Racist Doorman Instructions and Housing Application Coding System
description_short: Racist Doorman Instructions and Housing Application Coding System
description_medium: A 1973 Justice Department lawsuit alleged that Trump Management denied apartments to Black applicants or steered them to other buildings, and that employees marked Black applicants with codes. The case ended in a 1975 consent decree barring discriminatory rental practices without an admission of liability. The available case summary does not substantiate all the detailed staff instructions and effects asserted in the preserved long description.
description_long: Donald Trump implemented systematic housing discrimination by directing doormen and rental agents to mark Black applicant files with secret codes including 'C' for 'Colored' and 'No. 9' to identify African American families for automatic rental rejection across Trump Management properties, creating company-wide racist screening system that violated federal civil rights law. The comprehensive discrimination apparatus included training staff to lie about apartment availability when Black families inquired while maintaining detailed records of racial classifications designed to maintain segregated housing throughout Trump's 14,000-unit rental empire in New York City. The coding system extended beyond applications to include instructions for doormen to discourage Black visitors and prospective tenants through hostile treatment, verbal harassment, and misinformation about rental availability, effectively creating whites-only residential communities through systematic exclusion practices. Trump's racial discrimination violated constitutional equal protection principles by institutionalizing segregation through business operations while using coded language and secret documentation to circumvent civil rights enforcement, demonstrating sophisticated understanding of how to violate federal law while avoiding detection. The systematic exclusion created lasting trauma for Black families who were denied housing opportunities while Trump profited from maintaining artificially segregated communities that commanded higher rents through racial exclusivity, representing economic exploitation of racism for personal financial gain. The housing discrimination established Trump's foundational approach to civil rights and minority communities, demonstrating systematic willingness to violate federal law while using business operations as mechanisms for racial oppression and economic exploitation that would define his treatment of minority Americans throughout his career.
subcategory: Systematic Housing Discrimination and Racial Coding

title: Trump: Louis DeJoy starts at USPS, mail delays immediately follow
description_short: Trump: Louis DeJoy starts at USPS, mail delays immediately follow
description_medium: Louis DeJoy began as U.S. postmaster general on June 15, 2020. Within days, people reported mail delays, and later coverage described accumulated mail, delayed bills and veterans waiting for medication. The Postal Service was also preparing for election mail during the pandemic. The chronology links DeJoy’s arrival and complaints but does not establish that he caused every delay.
description_long: Louis DeJoy took office as U.S. postmaster general on June 15, 2020. The timeline says reports of mail delays appeared within a week, including accumulated mail, late bills and veterans waiting for medication. Broader media attention came about a month later, when the COVID-19 pandemic offered an apparent explanation for some disruption. The concern grew as the Postal Service prepared to handle increased election-related mail before the November presidential vote. The supplied account also places the complaints alongside rapid operational changes and quotes postal insiders who said the agency had generally avoided major changes close to a general election. Those details describe a period of disruption and heightened scrutiny, but they do not show that DeJoy caused every delayed delivery or that the changes were intended to affect voting. The practical stakes were whether the postal system could maintain ordinary service while managing pandemic-era demand and a large volume of mailed ballots. The timeline connects events in sequence; it does not establish a complete causal account of the delays.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: Louis DeJoy starts at USPS, mail delays immediately follow
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: Louis DeJoy starts at USPS, mail delays immediately follow

notes: The account describes timing and reported service problems but does not establish that DeJoy caused each delay or intended to obstruct election mail.

title: Donald Trump begins authoritarian attacks on the military
description_short: Donald Trump begins authoritarian attacks on the military
description_medium: At a Labor Day press event on September 7, 2020, Donald Trump criticized U.S. military leadership amid a report that he had called fallen service members “suckers.” The supplied account cuts off before giving Trump’s exact response or naming the officials he criticized, leaving the substance and target of the remarks unclear.

title: Donald Trump Jr. says it's time to go to ‘total war' over the election
description_short: Donald Trump Jr. says it's time to go to ‘total war' over the election
description_medium: Donald Trump Jr. says it's time to go to ‘total war' over the election. Donald Trump Jr. incites violence, stoking the militias that his father told to "stand by." We've filed this under "Illegal Activity" for inciting violence. Source https://twitter.com/DonaldJTrumpJr/status/1324473707121778688 Photo: Gage Skidmore This entry is cataloged as a standalone event because it captures a concrete action, public statement, legal development, documented relationship, or policy consequence linked directly or indirectly to Trump. The downstream effects include institutional stress, public-trust erosion, and accountability pressure across affected systems.
description_long: On November 5, 2020, Donald Trump Jr. posted on X urging his father to go to “total war” over the election. He said Donald Trump should expose what he alleged were fraud, cheating and votes by people who had died or no longer lived in the state, then called for “cleaning up this mess” so the country would not look like a “banana republic.” The post appeared while votes were still being counted after the presidential election. Its language urged an aggressive political response, but the tweet itself offered no evidence for the alleged fraud. It also contains no explicit call for physical violence or for militias to act. The preserved medium description characterizes the post as incitement and says it stoked militias, claims that go beyond the linked tweet. The tweet documents a public call to contest the election results; it does not substantiate the fraud claims it makes or establish the broader accusations in the preserved description.
